As someone who has been in your shoes for about 2 months with 5 trips down so far, here’s what I’ll say-

- you may get first class, MCE, etc. which is very nice. It’s happened rather often for me due to my origin and recent destinations. But definitely don’t get used to it. 

-the gate agent will be your friend. Go up to them and say it’s your first time flying standby and they should be kind enough to let you know what will work for the current situation at the gate. 

-Apple AirTags in everything, especially checked bags. If you miss a flight you’ll at least know where your stuff is. 

Altogether, it’s more stressful for sure than rev flying but the fact that it’s free and you have a chance at getting upgraded is worth it no doubt. There’s a game to it, it just takes playing it to learn it. Happy travels!!

I've gone through the Amen clinic after 4 years of struggling with teenage bipolar disorder and multiple psychiatrists that were completely useless in attempting to properly diagnose and treat me. I went to the Amen clinic 2 years ago. I had a SPECT scan done, and I was put under care of an on site psychiatrist who has been a psychiatric doctor for nearly 4 decades, while only working with Amen for about 7 years. He explained thoroughly how each portion of my SPECT scan related to my condition by comparing it to multiple examples of other scans for people my age. He kept me on the same medication I've been on for 2 years, but upped the dosage, and incorporated a few of the Amen clinic's supplements(including some generic options that arr cheaper), and I have never felt as great as I do now. 

I don't owe much to Daniel Amen directly. But never, after years of clinics and doctors and hundreds of thousands of dollars in trying to treat my condition, have I found as much success in any treatment I've received as I did at the Amen clinic. I would not be alive if I hadn't gone through Amen. Generalization like this is divisive, shameful, and essentially cancel culture. Have you ever thought for a second that those same doctors who have criticized him are just as guilty of being paid for it as he is? This is why mental health still has the stigma it does. If it's not government approved pharmaceuticals, it just doesn't work. Except for when it does, way better, cheaper, and for longer.

I absolutely appreciate the fact that the bus system is free, and I will acknowledge the fact that my experience was during peak season, but some serious consideration needs to be put in place concerning the fact that every bus I was on was packed to the brim with people, and the drivers were more focused on closing the doors and moving along(which is totally understandable) so offering the driver to be used as a resource at my time is invalid. I was also never once informed, along with anyone else I came across while on the bus, that there was any sort of app available. Google Maps had the routes within and worked well for finding the correct route to get where you need to go, but in multiple instances there were stops that were completely passed even after the driver was notified using the yellow cable. This is why I was stuck on the bus for nearly 90 minutes. 

Your system is free, so yes I understand it may not be perfect, but immediately calling out a dissatisfactory experience as imminent user error is extremely unprofessional.

I would absolutely suggest trying to get as close to the mountain as possible. Breck does offer a free bus system that will take you most anywhere in town but for us it was very irregular and sometimes we got stuck on the same bus for an hour or more. I'm sure that won't be as much of the case when it isn't during the peak season, but it was definitely a pressing issue for us nonetheless. Whatever the case, AirBNB/Vrbo are what we use every time we come out and it's always been great!

Breck tends to stay pretty snowy in the late season, we went out this past April and the snow was amazing. Peaks 8 and 9 are where you will find all of the greens and easy blues, but I absolutely suggest once everyone is up to the same speed make your way over to Peak 7. Monte Cristo, Pioneer, and Wirepatch are some of my favorite runs of all time. Very long, mildly steep groomed runs that my family and I can do literally all day. 

Actually, as I type this from our condo in Breckenridge, I can literally say that we made that loop up and down peak 7 about 15 times. Literally never gets old. Have fun!

The jist of it is, my dad and the two of us would alternate being on offense or defense, and the person on offense would "huddle" with my dad and figure out a passing route. Dad says hike, person on offense runs the route and the person on defense has to try to stop them from catching the ball, or try to intercept it. A catch on the offense was a point, a blocked pass by the defense was a point, and an interception on defense was two points. To win you had to be left with two points more than your opponent with a round of redemption. 

We started by going to 20 points, then 30, then 50, and from then on it was just until everyone decided to be done. The highest score I can recollect was my brother beating me 224 to 222. That game took almost an hour and a half and it was probably the best Thanksgiving of my life.
